title: Disc Jockeys, Except Radio
description: Play prerecorded music for live audiences at venues or events such as clubs, parties, or wedding receptions. May use techniques such as mixing, cutting, or sampling to manipulate recordings. May also perform as emcee (master of ceremonies).

clusters.label: Performing for or Working Directly with the Public

tasks.text: Accept music requests from event guests.
Encourage guests to dance using group dances, competitions, or other party games.
Lead party games, such as dance-offs or prize giveaways.
Create itemized invoices to record amounts due for services rendered.
Create tailored playlists by aligning music with event functions.
Mix, cut, or sample recorded music using DJ controllers, CDJs, or DJ mixers.
Select and play music incorporating crowd preferences and mood.
Operate disc jockey controller and other equipment, such as microphones.
Operate visual effects equipment, such as lights, fog machines, or lasers.

clusters.label: Estimating the Quantifiable Characteristics of Products, Events, or Information

tasks.text: Adhere to schedules to keep events running on time.
Advertise services using media such as internet advertising and brochures.
Communicate with clients or venue owners to determine event information, such as music preferences, scheduling, and anticipated attendance.
Conduct sound checks to ensure equipment is working and appropriate for the venue.
Listen to music before playing at events to ensure recordings are appropriate and meet quality standards.
Maintain up-to-date knowledge of music releases and trends.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Music or sound editing software
skills.def: Software to record or convert analog sounds to a digital format, or to apply effects such as fades, noise filtering, or volume adjustment. Examples: Adobe Audition, Audion Laboratories VoxPro, Avid Technology Pro Tools.
